answer_1.outputs: Reasoning chains (forward and backward) and answers

answer_2.quote: We evaluate REVTHINK on 12 diverse datasets across commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and natural language inference, using two models: Mistral-7B-Instruct and Gemma-7B-Instruct. Our results demonstrate that learning to think backward through our pipeline consistently improves performance, with an average gain of 13.53% over the student's zero-shot performance and 6.84% over the widely-used Symbolic Knowledge Distillation (SKD) method.
